notes: §1985:XII.2.4 GR5 (Amendment 2 applied): operands are tried in order at the leftmost library text word, a match "is equal, character for character, to the ordered sequence of library text words", comma, semicolon and space runs are one space, "Each lowercase letter is equivalent to the corresponding uppercase letter" (not inside a nonnumeric literal, §1985:III.2), an unmatched word is copied and matched text is never rescanned. ApplyReplacements scans TextWordScanner words with separator commas and semicolons dropped, tries the operands in written order and resumes after the rightmost matched word; TextWord#MatchesForReplacing compares words case-insensitively and nonnumeric literal content ordinally. Witness 1985-GR-XII_2_4-5 (ABCD). next.reason: Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993) added to 5b 'Each lowercase letter is equivalent to the corresponding uppercase letter as specified for the COBOL character set' (§1985:XII.2.4 GR5; that definition, §1985:III.2, excepts 'nonnumeric literals and some PICTURE symbols'), so case folding is no longer a 2023 addition: §2023:7.2.3.4 GR9 c) 3 has it 'Except when used in the non-hexadecimal formats of alphanumeric and national literals'. The comparison cycle is the same, but the operands differ. 1985 compares 'Pseudo-text-1, identifier-1, word-1, or literal-1'; 2023 compares 'pseudo-text-1 or partial-word-1' only (§2023:E.2: 'Removal of support for non-pseudo-text operands in the replacing phrase of the COPY statement') and adds partial matching, 'When the LEADING phrase is specified, partial-word-1 matches the library text only if', which 1985 refuses. 2023 also adds matching equivalences 1985's 'equal, character for character' lacks: 'each alphanumeric character is equivalent to its corresponding national character', 'The two representations of the quotation symbol match', and 'Each occurrence of a compiler directive line is treated as a single space'.
